line: Frank DeLuca. DeLuca Hardware, on Fifth, since my grandfather. If you've got a dripping tap, I've got the washer. Where's home for you?
Flu shot. My wife's idea. Frank DeLuca, the hardware store on Fifth. You look like you're waiting on somebody too.
choice1: Something like that. Nice to meet you.

line: I ask everybody. My grandfather came from Calabria with eleven words of English. By the time my dad was born, the Italian was gone. Nobody missed it.
choice2: That's one way to do it.

line: Maybe him, on Sundays. But he opened a store and the store fed four kids. You know what I ask of people at my counter? English at the counter, that's all I ask.
choice3: I'll let you get back to work.

line: At home, speak whatever you like. But a kid who sounds like he's from here gets the job. I've hired forty kids in thirty years. I'm telling you what I've seen.
choice1: Fair. You've seen a lot of kids.
choice2: A kid can sound like two places.

line: Kid came into the store yesterday asking for 'the thingy for the faucet.' I sold him the right thingy. That's thirty years of practice.
Returning my wife's mysteries. She reads one a day and blames me for the late fees. You use this place much?
You know what I like about you? You don't make a production of where you're from. You just show up. That's how my family did it.
choice2: Where I'm from isn't a production.

line: The Fifth Street merchants do a breakfast, first Friday. Bagels, bad coffee, the city's parking guy. I'd like you there. You'd be good for us.
You're turning into a regular around here. Come to the merchants' breakfast Friday. I'll introduce you as my friend. Better than a résumé.
Two agents came in Tuesday asking about a kid who used to sweep for me. I told them what I know: he's a good worker. That's all I know.
choice2: Did they say what they wanted?

line: The city wants signs in four languages now. Fine, I'll put them up. But I'll keep telling people the counter runs in English. It runs faster.
choice1: Signs won't slow the counter down.

line: Haven't seen you on Fifth in a while. Somebody said you're over on Grand most days. Don't get stuck in one corner of town, that's my advice.
choice1: Grand is part of town, Frank.

line: Ellen in 4C says you fixed her radiator valve. With a part from my store. Now that's how you get to be from somewhere.

choice1: Frank, about last time. No hard feelings?

line: Can't talk, I left the new kid alone at the register. Last time he sold a man forty feet of chain for the price of four.
